title: The Lost Sheep
writeup: A lone sheep walks out of a shallow stream toward the viewer while the shepherd and the rest of the flock wait on the path behind. Thick, sculpted paint gives the wool and the rocks a physical weight.
alt: A thickly painted sheep steps out of a shallow stream toward the viewer. A shepherd and the rest of the flock wait on the path behind, between trees.

title: The Lion and the Lamb
writeup: Jesus is referred to as the Lion of the Tribe of Judah and the Lamb who was slain.
alt: A split face in heavy paint: a lion in red and gold on the left, a lamb in thick cream wool on the right, held in a live-edge wooden frame.

title: The Lost Sheep (second version)
writeup: The sheep stands in the foreground, with the shepherd and the flock in the distance between tall trees and a bright sky. Bold knife-work colour runs through the water at its feet.
alt: A sheep stands in the foreground in brightly coloured water. Farther back, a shepherd and a flock stand between tall trees under a bright sky.

title: Unwavering
writeup: The woman with the issue of blood teaches us that when God gives us His attention, He is never multitasking. A faith as deep and unwavering as this woman’s not only earns God’s attention, but it also secures His undivided attention despite the multitude, voices, discouragement.
alt: A hand reaches through a crowd of robes built from thick red, green, and blue paint. A blue garment with a pale striped, fringed edge crosses the foreground.

title: Unwavering (framed version)
writeup: The woman with the issue of blood teaches us that when God gives us His attention, He is never multitasking. A faith as deep and unwavering as this woman’s not only earns God’s attention, but it also secures His undivided attention despite the multitude, voices, discouragement.
alt: The same reaching figure, painted more smoothly and set in an ornate gold frame. A blue garment sweeps across robes of red, green, and deep blue.

title: Bond
writeup:
In literature, music, and art, “backing a baby” is often used as a metaphor for unconditional support, protection, and resilience. It signifies a mother carrying the weight of the future, nurturing the next generation while continuing to move forward with strength and grace.

“A baby carried on the back doesn’t know how long the journey is.”

A proverb reflecting the absolute trust and rest a child finds in their mother.
alt: A woman in profile, built from geometric patterns, carries a baby on her back. The child is wrapped in a cloth of circles and stripes.
